title: A cost analysis challenges the claim that Kimi K3 is a bargain
friendlyTitle: Kimi K3 is powerful, but one analysis says it is not especially cheap
summary: An analysis using Artificial Analysis task costs argues that Moonshot AI’s open-weight Kimi K3 is only slightly cheaper per benchmark task than OpenAI’s top model, roughly twice the cost of GLM-5.2 and about 20 times DeepSeek V4. It notes that K3 is relatively cheaper for coding but more expensive for office work, partly because it produces longer outputs.
friendlySummary: A new comparison says Kimi K3 can cost nearly as much per completed task as a leading OpenAI model. It looks cheaper for coding and more expensive for office work.
whyItMatters: Token prices alone can hide how much a model costs to finish a task. Buyers comparing models should measure total tokens, latency and success on their own workload; open weights can still add value through fine-tuning or self-hosting even when hosted inference is not the cheapest.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A low price per token does not always mean a low price for the whole job. Test models on your real tasks, including how long their answers are and how often they succeed.
